items.markdown:
Glutathione is a powerful natural antioxidant used in skin care to `brighten tone, fade dark spots, and fight cellular aging`.[[1]](https://www.paulaschoice.com/expert-advice/skincare-advice/ingredient-spotlight/glutathione-for-skin.html)[[2]](https://www.vibrantskin.com/blogs/skincare/glutathione-for-skin)

### How It Works

- **Blocks pigment:** It stops the [tyrosinase](https://cosmoderma.org/glutathione-in-dermatology-a-bright-future-or-fading-hype/) enzyme from making melanin.
- **Shifts melanin type:** It changes dark brown melanin into lighter pigment.
- **Fights damage:** It neutralizes free radicals from UV rays and pollution.[[1]](https://skinnsuite.com/blog/does-glutathione-whiten-skin/)[[2]](https://www.vibrantskin.com/blogs/skincare/glutathione-for-skin)

### Benefits for Skin

- Fades hyperpigmentation, age spots, and melasma.
- Brightens dull complexions and evens out skin tone.
- Boosts elasticity and reduces fine lines by supporting collagen.[[1]](https://cosmoderma.org/glutathione-in-dermatology-a-bright-future-or-fading-hype/)[[2]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39444151/)[[3]](https://www.paulaschoice.com/expert-advice/skincare-advice/ingredient-spotlight/glutathione-for-skin.html)[[4]](https://skinnsuite.com/blog/does-glutathione-whiten-skin/)[[5]](https://www.vibrantskin.com/blogs/skincare/glutathione-for-skin)

### Delivery Methods & Efficacy

- **Topical creams and serums:** Generally safe and well-tolerated. Concentrations of 0.5% to 2% help reduce localized dark spots, though results take about 8 to 10 weeks of consistent use.[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11862975/)[[2]](https://www.paulaschoice.com/expert-advice/skincare-advice/ingredient-spotlight/glutathione-for-skin.html)[[3]](https://www.westlakedermatology.com/blog/glutathione-skincare-ingredient-focus/)[[4]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12710870/)[[5]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39444151/)[[6]](https://cosmoderma.org/glutathione-in-dermatology-a-bright-future-or-fading-hype/)
- **Oral supplements:** Doses of 250–500 mg daily offer mild, generalized brightening benefits, but absorption is limited and results are not permanent once stopped.[[1]](https://www.westlakedermatology.com/blog/glutathione-skincare-ingredient-focus/)[[2]](https://www.ovid.com/jnls/pigi/fulltext/10.4103/pigmentinternational.pigmentinternational_29_21~glutathione-the-master-antioxidant-beyond-skin-lightening)
- **Intravenous (IV) injections:** Highly controversial. While popular for rapid systemic effects, IV glutathione carries severe health risks—including liver damage, kidney dysfunction, and life-threatening allergic reactions—and lacks standardized safety approval.[[1]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41900080/)[[2]](https://cosmoderma.org/glutathione-in-dermatology-a-bright-future-or-fading-hype/)[[3]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11862975/)[[4]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40013212/)
